scenarios.title: Modern default: authenticated private NFSv4.2 read
scenarios.goal: Follow one ordinary read from a credentialed client to an accepted result, keeping authentication and permission distinct.
scenarios.profile: NFS-LINUX-R1: offline Linux-oriented standards illustration, revision2026-10-21. TCP; supported optional features explicitly fixed; no tested kernel/build claim. NFSv4.2 minorversion2, sec=krb5p, xprtsec=none. RPCSEC_GSSv1; Kerberos GSS OID1.2.840.113554.1.2.2, QOP0; symbolic enctype19 AES128-CTS-HMAC-SHA256-128; mutual authentication; no delegation.
actors: Linux NFS client and credential helper
NFS server with local policy store
preconditions: Fixed clock; Alice user TGT cached; separately provisioned machine credential; nfs/files.corp.example@CORP.EXAMPLE service key available only to the server/KDC.
Explicit export and a small named file policy fixture; v4.1 session bootstrap expanded via NFS06; delegations/pNFS off.
steps: Show local desktop UID, selected user cache, and selected machine identity in separate cards.
Request the nfs service ticket from the KDC; locally accept the TGS reply before making the ticket/context usable.
Establish the RPCSEC_GSS context using INIT and any genuinely needed continuation; server acceptance and client verification of mutual proof are distinct.
Complete supported client/session setup, then construct a minorversion2 user request for namespace traversal and OPEN.
Send a krb5p READ; retain protected wire data at receipt; locally unwrap/verify and validate replay/state before policy evaluation.
Evaluate mapped user, export and file policy; send the protected result; the client verifies it before displaying bytes. End with sourced CLOSE/context cleanup.
negativeCases: No user credential: stop at local context acquisition.
Invalid service-ticket key/version: reject context at the server.
Authenticated Alice lacks read permission: retain authentication success and deny file operation.
Corrupted protected result: client learns no file bytes.
acceptance: Default catalog entry selects NFS01, not v3.
No file content at either receiving endpoint before the relevant verification/unwrap event.
TGT never sent to NFS server; service key never acquired by client.
minorversion2 adds no invented login handshake; no v4.0-only bootstrap operations appear.

scenarios.title: Compare krb5, krb5i and krb5p
scenarios.goal: Compare the same READ at the same boundary under three independently scoped protection settings.
scenarios.profile: NFS-LINUX-R1: offline Linux-oriented standards illustration, revision2026-10-21. TCP; supported optional features explicitly fixed; no tested kernel/build claim. NFSv4.2; three fixed sec profiles; xprtsec=none. RPCSEC_GSSv1; Kerberos GSS OID1.2.840.113554.1.2.2, QOP0; symbolic enctype19 AES128-CTS-HMAC-SHA256-128; mutual authentication; no delegation.
actors: Linux NFS client and credential helper
NFS server with local policy store
preconditions: Reuse accepted context setup as an expandable prerequisite, never as unexplained magic.
Each comparison run has its own context, sequence numbers and packet generation.
steps: Present one protection map with RPC header, credential/verifier, procedure arguments and returned data as separate regions.
Construct and verify the header MIC for each service; show none/integrity/privacy body treatments from the pinned RFC2203 worksheet.
Run the same permitted READ through each receiver-local check.
Display which fields remain visible to a network observer and which exact endpoint operation exposes protected content.
negativeCases: Alter a procedure argument under krb5: show the absence of a body-integrity guarantee, not a fabricated MIC rejection.
Alter an integrity-protected body: receiver rejects it.
Alter privacy ciphertext: unwrap fails.
Repeat an already-used GSS sequence: no second dispatch; use the specification-defined discard behavior.
acceptance: Pseudo-flavor labels map to wire RPCSEC_GSS flavor6; no pseudo-flavor number is used as the RPC credential flavor.
Each displayed MIC has an explicit coverage list and source citation; do not claim whole IP/TCP encryption.
Corruption demonstrates the selected mode, not a blanket red failure for all modes.
At least header verifier, body and sequence number have exact operational field replay.

scenarios.title: NFSv3: client-asserted identity and root squashing
scenarios.goal: Explain the separate mount path and the trust placed in client-supplied numeric identities.
scenarios.profile: NFS-LINUX-R1: offline Linux-oriented standards illustration, revision2026-10-21. TCP; supported optional features explicitly fixed; no tested kernel/build claim. NFSv3/MOUNTv3; sec=sys; xprtsec=none; explicit root_squash, anonuid65534/anongid65534.
actors: NFS service and local filesystem policy
preconditions: Configured export, fixed service endpoints and numeric identity namespace.
No KDC/context/certificate is implied; privileged-port policy, if displayed, is a separate fixture assumption.
steps: Send MOUNTv3 MNT for the named export; local export decision produces filehandle and allowed auth flavors.
Client receives the mount result; show that it is not a grant to read every file.
Build NFSv3 LOOKUP/READ using AUTH_SYS stamp, machine-name, UID, primary GID and groups.
At server receipt label the identity client asserted; perform configured squashing and file-policy checks.
Return data or the sourced NFSv3 error; compare an ordinary caller with a UID/GID0 caller.
negativeCases: Export disallows client: mount denied.
UID0 maps to anonymous identity and file access is denied.
Same numeric UID names different people on two hosts: expose the namespace collision.
Forged client assertion is not magically detected cryptographically.
acceptance: No v4 COMPOUND/session/stateid appears.
Root squash is visibly a mapping policy, not proof of user identity or a complete defense against all forged UIDs.
A filehandle possession test cannot bypass the file-policy evaluator.
All fields survive exact receipt/history inspection without being mislabeled verified credentials.

scenarios.title: NFSv3 can use Kerberos
scenarios.goal: Demonstrate that version3 is not synonymous with AUTH_SYS.
scenarios.profile: NFS-LINUX-R1: offline Linux-oriented standards illustration, revision2026-10-21. TCP; supported optional features explicitly fixed; no tested kernel/build claim. NFSv3/MOUNTv3; sec=krb5i; xprtsec=none. RPCSEC_GSSv1; Kerberos GSS OID1.2.840.113554.1.2.2, QOP0; symbolic enctype19 AES128-CTS-HMAC-SHA256-128; mutual authentication; no delegation.
actors: Linux NFS client and credential helper
NFS server with local policy store
preconditions: NFS03 discovery skeleton, NFS service principal/key and valid user credentials.

Fixed MOUNT profile uses explicitly labeled AUTH_SYS discovery and advertises configured Kerberos pseudo-flavor; this discovery has no cryptographic integrity. The client pins krb5i as its minimum and never treats advertisement as proof.
steps: Obtain the initial filehandle and flavor advertisement through the MOUNTv3 profile.
Select krb5i by local policy; obtain/reuse an nfs service ticket and establish a mutual GSS context.
Issue NFSv3 READ with RPCSEC_GSS header/body protection.
Server verifies, maps and authorizes; client validates the response before using it.
negativeCases: MOUNT advertisement lacks a locally allowed flavor: no silent sys downgrade.
Wrong service target or failed mutual proof: no accepted context.
User ticket expires: context reacquisition follows the selected lifetime profile, not a KDC exchange per READ.
acceptance: Align milestones with NFS03 and highlight only changed security portions.
Keep MOUNT success distinct from authenticated NFS data access.
No forwarding of the TGT/password; use flavor6 on the data RPC.

scenarios.title: NFSv4.0: integrated namespace and state
scenarios.goal: Explain what changed from v3 while avoiding a claim that v4 itself encrypts or authenticates users.
scenarios.profile: NFS-LINUX-R1: offline Linux-oriented standards illustration, revision2026-10-21. TCP; supported optional features explicitly fixed; no tested kernel/build claim. NFSv4.0 minorversion0; default sec=krb5p, named sec=sys comparison; delegations off.
actors: Linux NFS client and credential helper
NFS server with local policy store
preconditions: Version-specific operation worksheet; existing credential setup reused only for the Kerberos branch.
Explicitly configured server accepts the selected flavor.
steps: Traverse the integrated namespace without a separate MOUNT RPC.
For the secure branch, establish user GSS context and show separately scoped client-state identity.
Use SETCLIENTID and SETCLIENTID_CONFIRM where required by the selected v4.0 trace, then OPEN/READ/CLOSE with version-correct state handling.
Compare the AUTH_SYS branch at the same permission decision; render its identity assurance accurately.
negativeCases: Server policy refuses sys: stop at the sourced security boundary.
Missing client-state credential: fail setup, not Alice password validation.
Invalid/expired state input: show a state error independently of valid user authentication.
acceptance: No EXCHANGE_ID, CREATE_SESSION or SEQUENCE in v4.0.
Keep GSS handle, clientid, filehandle and stateid visually distinct.
Capability-to-implement Kerberos is not narrated as mandatory selection on every mount.
A future delegation variant must separately source the callback direction; it is not silently included here.

scenarios.title: NFSv4.1: machine state and user access
scenarios.goal: Make machine protection of client/session state distinct from Alice’s file permissions.
scenarios.profile: NFS-LINUX-R1: offline Linux-oriented standards illustration, revision2026-10-21. TCP; supported optional features explicitly fixed; no tested kernel/build claim. NFSv4.1 minorversion1; standards profile explicitly negotiates SP4_MACH_CRED with integrity protection and fixed must_enforce/must_allow bitmaps; no universal Linux-default claim.
actors: Linux NFS client and credential helper
NFS server with local policy store
preconditions: Machine context and Alice context have separate identities and generations.
Server supports the selected state-protection option; the returned operation bitmap is fixed and displayed.
steps: Establish the machine GSS context and submit EXCHANGE_ID; expand its selected protection policy.
Accept the returned client identity only after checking the reply.
Send CREATE_SESSION under the required identity; record accepted session and slot state.
Create/reuse the separate user context and issue a SEQUENCE-prefixed OPEN/READ.
Display machine-state permission and user-file permission side by side at the final decision.
negativeCases: Wrong machine principal tries protected maintenance: reject at that operation.
Valid machine context but missing Alice context: no Alice READ.
Unsupported protection selection: explicit negotiation failure, no silent downgrade.
acceptance: Scripted tests exercise returned bitmap semantics instead of assuming every operation uses the machine credential.
No file permission is inferred from possession of clientid/sessionid.
Two users can have separate contexts on the modeled client; do not give one user the other’s cache.
Show RPC GSS sequence and NFS slot/sequence as different counters.

scenarios.title: Recover from a security-policy boundary
scenarios.goal: Show how a client discovers an acceptable security tuple without silently weakening local policy.
scenarios.profile: NFS-LINUX-R1: offline Linux-oriented standards illustration, revision2026-10-21. TCP; supported optional features explicitly fixed; no tested kernel/build claim. NFSv4.1; fixed namespace crossing; SECINFO and supported SECINFO_NO_NAME; default krb5i to required krb5p.
actors: Linux NFS client and credential helper
NFS server with local policy store
preconditions: One export boundary with a fixed allowed tuple list; explicit client minimum protection.
No authentication policy selected solely from response order; source version-specific operation/error rules.
steps: Issue the fixed namespace request under the insufficient tuple.
Return NFS4ERR_WRONGSEC only at the worksheet’s legal operation boundary.
Query SECINFO by component name; provide SECINFO_NO_NAME as a bounded alternate trace.
Client evaluates mechanism OID/QOP/service and chooses an allowed tuple, then retries the operation.
Complete the same user-mapping and file checks; security discovery alone grants nothing.
negativeCases: No common tuple satisfying local policy: stop denied.
Tampered unauthenticated discovery is not treated as proof; strict minimum remains enforced.
A following operation mistakenly uses a consumed filehandle: fail the fixture’s structural validation.
acceptance: Tests assert actual operation/error pairs, not generic wrongsec text on READ.
The v4.1 SECINFO filehandle consumption difference is represented in state.
No mixed list of unmodeled flavors and no uncontrolled retry loop.
Tuple, policy minimum and final selection are inspectable and replayable where operational.

scenarios.title: From principal to UID/GID to access decision
scenarios.goal: Explain why successful Kerberos authentication can still end in permission denial.
scenarios.profile: NFS-LINUX-R1: offline Linux-oriented standards illustration, revision2026-10-21. TCP; supported optional features explicitly fixed; no tested kernel/build claim. NFSv4.2/krb5p; explicit local principal map and filesystem adapter; named AUTH_SYS squash comparison.
actors: Linux NFS client and credential helper
NFS server with local policy store
preconditions: Fixture declares principal→local-ID/group mapping and owner/owner_group display mapping separately.
Use a named synthetic permission model; distinguish Linux POSIX mode/ACL projection from the RFC NFSv4 ACE model rather than pretending they are identical.
steps: Accept authenticated alice@CORP.EXAMPLE through the existing GSS helper.
Resolve the configured authorization identity and groups locally; disclose the fixture mapping.
Read owner/owner_group metadata and apply a separate display mapping.
Evaluate export host/flavor/read-only rules, any configured squash mapping, and file authorization.
Explain the first denying rule or permitted operation; return the appropriate protected result.
negativeCases: Unmapped authenticated principal follows the explicitly configured deny policy.
Owner-name display mapping fails while authenticated READ still succeeds.
Read-only export denies write; file ACL independently denies another operation.
Numeric identity collision or unauthorized group membership is visible, not corrected by inventing a KDC exchange.
acceptance: Kerberos realm, DNS name, NFSv4 identity domain and local UID are separate fields.
Policy evidence lists the effective caller and first denying rule, without requiring the beginner to inspect JSON.
Root-squash/all-squash variants name their exact anonymous IDs and affected scope.
NFS ACCESS is a request-specific result, never an irrevocable future access token.

scenarios.title: A non-domain-joined Linux workstation uses Kerberos
scenarios.goal: Answer how a locally logged-on user accesses a realm-protected NFS share without assuming domain join.
scenarios.profile: NFS-LINUX-R1: offline Linux-oriented standards illustration, revision2026-10-21. TCP; supported optional features explicitly fixed; no tested kernel/build claim. NFSv4.2/krb5p; MIT Kerberos1.22 documentation profile; manually provisioned realm configuration and host credential; no domain-join operation.
actors: Linux NFS client and credential helper
NFS server with local policy store
preconditions: Local desktop identity workstation/alex differs from explicitly selected alice@CORP.EXAMPLE.
Reachable KDC, trustworthy service-name configuration, time alignment, mapped server account, and a separately provisioned machine keytab for this Linux v4 profile.
User cache location/type is supported by the chosen helper; no assumption that any arbitrary credential cache is discovered.
steps: Show nonjoined state and manually configured realm/service mapping.
Acquire Alice’s TGT through explicit kinit-style sign-in; cross-link the existing Kerberos AS lesson instead of reimplementing PKINIT/FAST here.
Obtain the service ticket and initialize user GSS context.
Show the separate machine credential required by the chosen client-state path, then resume NFS01.
Server authenticates the selected realm principal and checks its own mapping/export/file policy.
negativeCases: User TGT exists but required machine keytab is absent: stop at machine/state setup.
Local UID maps to a different credential cache: no implicit use of Alice’s ticket.
Wrong realm/service name or KDC unreachable: credential acquisition failure.
Authentication succeeds but mapping or file policy denies access.
acceptance: The result says join is not the protocol proof; it does not say kinit always suffices.
No join-derived trust or SPN registration is silently fabricated.
No claim rpc.gssd -n removes machine-state credential requirements.
A compact v3 comparison may omit v4 state requirements, but is not an escape hatch presented as a universal modern setup.

scenarios.title: Add a connection without inventing a new user login
scenarios.goal: Separate NFS session binding and replay control from authentication and filesystem authorization.
scenarios.profile: NFS-LINUX-R1: offline Linux-oriented standards illustration, revision2026-10-21. TCP; supported optional features explicitly fixed; no tested kernel/build claim. NFSv4.1/4.2 standards profile; one server, two TCP connections; SP4_MACH_CRED requires BIND_CONN_TO_SESSION in returned must_enforce bitmap; no pNFS/trunking topology expansion.
actors: Linux NFS client and credential helper
NFS server with local policy store
preconditions: Accepted NFS06 session and fixed state-protection policy; same server identity verified by the profile.
Existing user GSS context and a deterministic outstanding request/slot fixture.
steps: Open a second connection and bind it using the required protected machine context.
Server checks binding conditions before associating it with the existing session; client verifies the response before marking connection usable.
Send an ordinary user request through the added connection; apply user authorization as before.
Demonstrate a lost response and permitted session replay using a fresh acceptable GSS RPC sequence with the same NFS slot request.
negativeCases: Possession of sessionid without required proof does not bind a connection.
Wrong principal or invalid proof fails before connection usability.
Replayed GSS sequence is rejected/discarded by GSS handling; a distinct valid session retry returns the recorded result.
One connection fails: display surviving session state only where the selected trace permits it.
acceptance: No copied SMB binding flags, SMB signing keys or automatic KDC exchange per connection.
Test no duplicate application side effect and no privilege gain.
Failed binding does not manufacture usable connection state.
Name NFS session binding, GSS/TLS channel binding and TLS session as three distinct concepts.

scenarios.title: RPC-with-TLS protects a transport, not a user claim
scenarios.goal: Explain server-only versus mutual host authentication while preserving AUTH_SYS’s identity limits.
scenarios.profile: NFS-LINUX-R1: offline Linux-oriented standards illustration, revision2026-10-21. TCP; supported optional features explicitly fixed; no tested kernel/build claim. NFSv4.2/TCP; sec=sys; default xprtsec=mtls, named tls comparison; TLS1.3 RFC9846; TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, X25519, ECDSA P-256 certificate signatures (ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256), no resumption/0-RTT.
actors: Server RPC/TLS endpoint and export policy
preconditions: TLS helper configured, explicit trust and host authorization policy.
Visible server/client certificate identities; different endpoint private-key handles.
Apply the ALPN discrepancy disposition in the source notes before coding the wire flight.
steps: Use the RPC NULL procedure with empty AUTH_TLS credential and empty AUTH_NONE verifier. Accept only MSG_ACCEPTED with an AUTH_NONE verifier containing the eight ASCII octets STARTTLS; then start TLS on that same TCP connection. The probe accept_stat is not itself the TLS-support criterion.
Perform TLS1.3, including the server request for a client identity; tls may accept no client certificate, mtls requires the selected valid identity.
Separate certificate receipt, local handshake-key derivation/decryption, certificate/proof validation and established transport.
Carry AUTH_SYS RPC in application-data ciphertext, followed by receiver-local decoded RPC.
Show two client user IDs on the same host transport; apply export/squash/file policy independently for each.
negativeCases: Client certificate absent in required-mtls profile: transport not admitted.
Valid client certificate but host unauthorized: no accepted association.
Valid TLS with forged UID: no invented user-identity proof.
Corrupted application-data record: no decoded RPC or file effect.
acceptance: Only outer TLS record is visible on wire; decoded RPC appears at the receiver’s actual decrypt event.
No HTTPS wrapping or separate invented NFS-TLS port.
Each endpoint derives its own directional traffic-secret objects; private keys never move.
TLS-only and mTLS badges describe hosts; sec=sys remains client-asserted user identity.

scenarios.title: Required transport protection fails closed
scenarios.goal: Locate failures before NFS access rather than misreporting them as a user-password error.
scenarios.profile: NFS-TLS-STRICT-R1, revision2026-10-21. Reuse NFS11 TLS profile with fixed xprtsec=mtls and no cleartext fallback.
preconditions: A single failure input changes one condition; retain the same declared protection policy.
Certificate validation includes the chosen identity/use/time/revocation policy; offline revocation outcomes are synthetic, not live OCSP claims.
steps: Attempt the NFS11 discovery/handshake until the selected failure detector.
Record the actual failing protocol/local-policy stage and the client’s observation.
Stop the selected connection/mount attempt; keep the request undispatched and application data unavailable.
Show a concise repair hint tied to that cause; an opportunistic comparison, if displayed, is a separate explicitly labeled policy.
negativeCases: Unsupported/malformed AUTH_TLS reply: do not send ClientHello.
Wrong server name or untrusted/expired certificate: validation fails.
Missing/incompatible sunrpc ALPN: no accepted RPC transport.
mTLS-required client identity missing or invalid; selected revocation check rejects.
acceptance: No cleartext retry under strict policy.
No phantom GSS failure or NFS wrong-password error.
Client-side failure knowledge follows actual response/local validation; no instantaneous shared global status.
Retry/reset cannot reuse rejected transport keys as an established channel.

scenarios.title: Advanced: bind user GSS authentication to TLS
scenarios.goal: Keep host transport authentication and user GSS authentication distinct, with an explicit binding check.
scenarios.profile: NFS-GSS-TLS-STANDARDS-R1, revision2026-10-21. Standards-only followup; one user GSS mechanism instance on one TLS1.3 connection; implementation support unverified.
actors: Linux NFS client and credential helper
NFS server with local policy store
preconditions: Source-confirm and pin the exact RPCSEC_GSS/channel-binding profile before implementation; do not call a generic Linux sec=krb5 mount a verified binding implementation.
Use a single GSS context per teaching transport; no multiuser shared-binding generalization.
steps: Finish the NFS11 TLS handshake and locally derive tls-exporter binding data at each endpoint.
Use RFC9266 exporter label EXPORTER-Channel-Binding, zero-length context and 32-byte output; label the result binding data, not an application encryption key.
Establish the user GSS context with the pinned binding interface and demonstrate endpoint comparison.
Carry the selected RPC protection inside TLS; authorization still uses the authenticated user.
End the upper-layer exchange and close the teaching connection; do not reuse the binding for another mechanism instance.
negativeCases: Different TLS connection supplies different binding: reject before usable user context.
TLS valid but GSS user proof invalid: retain transport success, deny user authentication.
Selected implementation lacks required binding interface: unsupported capability, not a silently weakened success.
acceptance: Evidence includes the exact implementation or a conspicuous standards-only badge.
TLS traffic secrets, binding value and GSS context keys are distinct objects.
RFC9266 section4.1 instance/lifetime restrictions are explicitly checked.
No universal RPCSEC_GSSv3, Linux or Windows support claim.

scenarios.title: Workgroup workstation: local password logon
scenarios.goal: Follow a local account from credential collection through SAM validation, interactive-logon authorization and a usable desktop; show where an access token first exists.
actors: A: LSA/LSASS authentication and policy role
P: user process/session and kernel token role
preconditions: Windows11 supported Enterprise/Pro reference; workgroup PC WORKGROUPPC; LOCAL bob is a standard user.
Password provider; no domain, cloud account, Hello or automatic sign-in; local policy permits console logon.

steps.action: Select WORKGROUPPC\bob and enter the synthetic password. Credential collection is not authentication.
steps.boundary: No authenticated identity or token yet.

steps.action: Submit the declared interactive-logon request and selected authentication package.
steps.boundary: Local IPC, never an HTTP/NTLM challenge exchange.

steps.action: The local package validates the submitted credential against the SAM account authority and returns account/group data.
steps.boundary: Only S/A learn verification success at their actual boundaries.

steps.action: Evaluate console logon rights and account restrictions, then form the new logon session and primary token.
steps.boundary: Authentication alone does not bypass an explicit deny right.

steps.action: Attach the token to userinit/shell startup, load the selected profile, then mark desktop ready.
steps.boundary: Token availability precedes successful profile/desktop startup.

steps.action: Evaluate one declared file DACL with this token; record grant separately from sign-in.
steps.boundary: A signed-in user can still be denied a file.

negativeCases.condition: Local verifier mismatch
negativeCases.preserved: No token/desktop; no DC traffic.

negativeCases.condition: Selected account disabled
negativeCases.preserved: No success result.

negativeCases.condition: SeDenyInteractiveLogonRight applies despite valid password
negativeCases.preserved: Credential verification remains historical; no successful console session.

negativeCases.condition: Profile startup fails after token creation
negativeCases.preserved: Authentication history remains; desktopReady=false.

acceptance: Every named actor/store is local; zero network messages in this profile.
Token contains a synthetic local user SID, attributed group SIDs, privilege list with enabled flags, logon identifier and integrity label; no password or Kerberos ticket embedded.
Credential-input buffers receive a declared cleanup event; durable verifier and token have different owners/lifetimes.
No token exists at credential receipt or before authority/policy checks.

scenarios.title: Domain-member workstation: online AD DS password logon
scenarios.goal: Connect local Windows sign-in to actual Kerberos AS/TGS work, local workstation service-ticket validation, and locally created access tokens.
actors: A: LSA/LSASS authentication and policy role
P: user process/session and kernel token role
M: workstation machine credential and local Kerberos acceptor
preconditions: WORKSTATION is an ADDS member; CORP\alice exists; DC/DNS/time and machine relationship work.
Select AES password preauthentication; no NTLM fallback in this fixture; FAST disabled only to isolate WLOG06.
Pin current supported Windows11 client, Server2025 KDC, policy and complete MS-KILE revision; logical roles are not separate external servers.

steps.action: Collect explicitly scoped CORP\alice input and submit to the local Kerberos authentication package.
steps.boundary: LSASS submission is not a network request.

steps.action: Run existing AS request/reply model, including selected preauth metadata, client-derived key and KDC-owned authoritative key.
steps.boundary: No clear password crosses the KDC leg.

steps.action: Decrypt and validate the client part before acquiring the issued TGT session key and installing the opaque TGT.
steps.boundary: Ticket receipt is distinct from usable credential acquisition.

steps.action: Request host/workstation.corp.example for the workstation itself and validate its TGS reply.
steps.boundary: Do not stop the sign-in explanation at receiving a TGT.

steps.action: The workstation Kerberos runtime interprets its host ticket and validated authorization data using its own service identity.
steps.boundary: This is local workstation processing, not a fabricated network AP exchange to another host.

steps.action: Combine validated domain identity/group information with local policy/alias membership and logon rights; create the primary token and start the session.
steps.boundary: Token issued locally, not sent by KDC.

steps.action: Offer a separate network-resource lesson using the retained credential context.
steps.boundary: Desktop success does not authorize a share/file.

negativeCases.condition: Preauthentication fails
negativeCases.preserved: No accepted user TGT or local token.

negativeCases.condition: Time or workstation service target invalid
negativeCases.preserved: No invented local success; retain prior valid credential history where applicable.

negativeCases.condition: Ticket cannot be accepted by the selected machine identity
negativeCases.preserved: TGT receipt is not a desktop grant.

negativeCases.condition: Domain authentication succeeds but local deny right applies
negativeCases.preserved: No usable desktop; no arbitrary cached bypass.

negativeCases.condition: Account requires change before authentication completes
negativeCases.preserved: Explicit stop/cross-link; do not invent an inline password-change protocol.

acceptance: Assert AS/TGS target, key owner, reply receipt/acceptance and local-token boundaries.
No domain password transmitted to SAM, no SAM verifier masquerading as an AES key, and no user token copied out of a TGT.
Token provenance lists domain identity/group facts separately from local aliases/privileges and application access decisions.
Do not teach arbitrary Kerberos-error-to-NTLM fallback; a future compatibility branch needs its own sourced condition and carrier.

scenarios.goal: Demonstrate a previously signed-in domain user entering a disconnected desktop and distinguish cached validation from fresh domain authentication and network credentials.

steps: Resolve the entered local account to UID, GID, groups, home and shell; label this identity lookup rather than proof of identity.

negativeCases: Unknown user; incorrect password; authenticated account denied; session setup failure.

scenarios.title: polkit: authorize one privileged operation
scenarios.goal: Explain a service authorization decision, its optional authentication challenge and the service action that follows.
preconditions: Profile L-POLKIT: one real action ID, action details and pinned policy; declare local/active session and available agent.

steps: Client requests an operation from the privileged mechanism.
Mechanism asks polkit about the subject and exact action.
Return deny, allow, auth_self or auth_admin according to explicit policy.
For a challenge, the agent authenticates an allowed identity through the native backend and reports the result through the privileged path.
Authority completes the authorization decision; mechanism alone performs the allowed operation.

scenarios.title: Mac Platform SSO: registration, login policy and IdP identity
scenarios.goal: Explain managed Platform SSO without treating local login, IdP authentication and account privilege as one token exchange.
preconditions: Profile M-PSSO: pin macOS version, IdP/extension version and exact configuration. Baseline covers password and Secure Enclave key methods as alternative branches.
State device registration, user registration and local-account creation status; capture configured offline/login policy.
steps: Show device and user registration dependencies and the established local-account association.
Select the configured method and login policy; show local password handling separately from IdP proof.
Password method: apply the configured online requirement/offline allowance and password synchronization outcome.
Secure Enclave key method: retain the local-password login boundary and show a separate hardware-key IdP authentication operation.
Record the resulting local session and separate IdP SSO state, then link application-token use.
Expose version-specific optional methods only when the extension and current Apple capability table support them.
negativeCases: Registration incomplete; IdP unreachable under required-online policy; unsupported method; failed remote proof; disabled/exempt account mismatch.
acceptance: Do not draw proprietary IdP messages without that provider specification and captured version.
Required-online and offline-grace branches must be causally different.
Gate newer web/QR/required-Touch-ID behavior to documented macOS 27 support; earlier availability of Platform SSO alone is insufficient.

scenarios.title: Mac administrator authorization for a scoped GUI operation
scenarios.goal: Explain operation-specific authorization without turning the whole desktop or application into root.
preconditions: Profile M-AUTHZ: one supported privileged operation and its actual authorization right/policy; local administrator baseline.
This models OS behavior; do not implement a native privileged helper or use deprecated AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges.
steps: Request a named operation and its authorization right.
Evaluate the right and decide whether an eligible administrator must authenticate.
Obtain an allowed administrator identity, which may differ from the logged-in user.
Validate required authentication and grant only the operation/right scope defined by policy.
Privileged component verifies authorization and performs the operation; client identity remains unchanged.
Release the authorization reference or show bounded reuse only where the chosen right permits it.
negativeCases: Correct standard-user password insufficient; prompt canceled; right denied; different operation not covered; stale or invalid authorization.
acceptance: Separate requester, authenticated administrator and executing service identities.
Optional Touch ID/Apple Watch approval appears only for a documented supported prompt and configured hardware/account state; no synthetic wireless protocol.
No global root token, secure token, TGT or FileVault entitlement is created by this approval.

scenarios.goal: Show macOS command elevation as sudo policy plus its actual PAM/authentication configuration.
preconditions: Profile M-SUDO: record OS build, bundled sudo version and effective /etc/pam.d/sudo include chain.
Password baseline; Touch ID is an explicit supported/configured branch using Apple pam_tid, not assumed enabled everywhere.
steps: Choose caller, command and target identity; evaluate sudo authorization.
Check timestamp scope and whether fresh authentication is needed.
Password branch invokes its configured provider; Touch ID branch identifies the PAM user and asks the local system for the permitted verification.
Accept the method result only through the selected stack; fallback is explicit stack behavior.
Run the allowed command with target credentials and retain the invoking desktop identity.
Expire/invalidate authentication reuse and clean up transient state.
negativeCases: Policy denies despite biometric success; no eligible local UI/session; canceled or failed verification; unsupported module/configuration; timestamp expires.
acceptance: Reuse LELEV01 policy/timestamp concepts while retaining an independent macOS implementation profile.

scenarios.title: Mac Platform SSO network administrator authorization
scenarios.goal: Show the distinct case where an IdP identity without a local account can authorize a supported administrator prompt.
preconditions: Profile M-PSSO-NETADMIN: supported macOS/extension, shared device keys and explicitly configured administrator/group mappings.
Choose an operation eligible for network authorization; it must not require secure token, volume ownership or authentication specifically by the current local user.
steps: Start a supported authorization request under an existing local session.
Select the allowed network-only identity and authenticate through the configured provider.
Evaluate the returned group/privilege mapping and requested right.
Grant the scoped authorization and perform the operation without creating a local user merely to label the network identity.
Compare a secure-token/ownership-specific operation, which must select a different eligible authorization path or fail.
negativeCases: IdP unavailable; administrator group mapping absent; network identity authentication succeeds but right denied; operation requires excluded local/ownership credentials.
acceptance: Network-only administrator proof does not manufacture a secure token, volume ownership or a workstation login session.
Keep the IdP mapping policy inspectable and show only the documented provider exchange.
This is a separate authorization capability from ordinary Platform SSO login, not a renamed local-administrator scenario.

scenarios.title: JWT, JWS, JWE and opaque tokens
scenarios.goal: Separate token representation from the protocol, protection and authorization decision.
preconditions: Three fixed synthetic examples; no real credentials; compact serialization explicitly selected.

steps.action: Create a signed three-segment JWT, encrypted five-segment JWT, and opaque reference token.
steps.heldState: Issuer owns source claims; each output has its own exact artifact ID.

steps.action: Let the holder decode JWS header/payload, inspect JWE envelope only, and view opaque bytes only.
steps.heldState: Decoded JWS claims remain unverified; JWE plaintext is absent at holders without the decryption key.

steps.action: Route each artifact to its configured validation path.
steps.heldState: Parsing creates no authenticated identity or access grant.

steps.action: Show protection and validator panels side by side.
steps.heldState: JWT is a claims format; JWS gives integrity, JWE confidentiality/integrity; opaque is a client representation, not inherently weaker.

negativeCases: Malformed segment/base64url/JSON input produces a parse error before trust state.
Do not infer token format merely from an OAuth response field name.
acceptance: Inspection never labels base64url decoding as decryption.
Do not state that every JWS is a JWT, every JWT is encrypted, or JWT itself is an authentication protocol.

scenarios.title: Signed JWT verification and tampering
scenarios.goal: Show exactly what signature verification establishes and what still needs checking.
preconditions: RS256 demo profile with a pinned trusted issuer key; source bytes and encoded signing input retained.

steps.action: Issuer signs BASE64URL(header).BASE64URL(payload).
steps.heldState: Private signing key remains at issuer; public verification key is verifier-local.

steps.action: API receives the exact compact token over the selected TLS carrier.
steps.heldState: Inbox holds received bytes and untrusted decoded claims.

steps.action: Verify signature with configured key and algorithm.
steps.heldState: A local signature-valid observation references the same token generation.

steps.action: Run issuer/audience/time/profile checks before policy.
steps.heldState: Only all-success creates validatedClaims; access still requires separate policy.

negativeCases: Flip one payload byte or signature byte: verification fails.
A correctly signed token for another API must still fail contextual validation.
acceptance: No private key is delivered to client or verifier.
Failure creates no accepted identity; exact-history shows receive, parse, verify and claim acceptance separately.

scenarios.title: Encrypted and nested JWT acceptance
scenarios.goal: Explain decryption, AEAD validation and inner signature validation as distinct steps.
preconditions: Explicit sign-then-encrypt profile; outer alg RSA-OAEP-256 and enc A128GCM; inner signed JWT; cty JWT.

steps.action: Create inner signed JWT, then encrypt it to the recipient public key.
steps.heldState: Issuer keeps signing secret; recipient alone holds private decryption key; CEK has explicit local custody.

steps.action: Deliver JWE compact envelope.
steps.heldState: Carrier and recipient inbox inspect ciphertext; no automatically acquired plaintext.

steps.action: Validate encryption parameters and authentication tag, then expose inner bytes locally.
steps.heldState: Authenticated decryption creates recipient-local inner JWS; claims still lack issuer acceptance.

steps.action: Verify inner signature and expected JWT profile claims.
steps.heldState: Separate decrypt-valid, signature-valid and claims-valid observations precede use.

negativeCases: Wrong recipient key or changed tag produces no plaintext acquisition.
Valid outer JWE with invalid inner signature is rejected; encryption alone does not prove sender identity.
acceptance: Never perform encrypt-then-skip-signature acceptance.
Clarify compact segment counts are serialization-specific; JWE is not the Kubernetes human-token profile.

scenarios.title: Algorithm and key-type confusion rejected
scenarios.goal: Make algorithm policy an input to verification, not a value chosen by the attacker.
preconditions: Demo verifier allowlist RS256 only; keys bound to algorithm and purpose; no unsigned-token use case.

steps.action: Install trusted algorithm/key profile before token arrival.
steps.heldState: Verifier owns immutable profile revision.

steps.action: Read untrusted alg header and candidate key metadata.
steps.heldState: Header is a hint, not authorization to select any primitive.

steps.action: Reject none, unexpected HS256, key-type mismatch or incompatible use/key_ops.
steps.heldState: Failure references the rejecting constraint before any trusted-claims state.

steps.action: Allow matching RS256 candidate through cryptographic verification and contextual checks.
steps.heldState: Only successful checks create acceptance.

negativeCases: RSA public bytes must never become an HMAC shared secret.
Unknown critical header extension is rejected if the profile cannot process it.
acceptance: Selected algorithm and allowlist visible together; no silent downgrade.
Do not imply RFC 7519 universally bans unsecured JWTs; this accepting profile explicitly does.

scenarios.title: Issuer trust, discovery, kid and JWKS
scenarios.goal: Explain where trusted verification keys come from and what kid does not prove.
preconditions: Fixed issuer https://issuer.demo.example; HTTPS trust; issuer-scoped JWKS cache; asymmetric public keys only.

steps.action: Fetch configured issuer metadata and check returned issuer equals expected issuer.
steps.heldState: Verifier stores a validated metadata revision and trusted jwks_uri.

steps.action: Retrieve JWKS from that trusted URI.
steps.heldState: Verifier caches public verification candidates; issuer private keys never leave issuer.

steps.action: Use kid as an untrusted selector within this issuer key set; filter type, purpose and algorithm.
steps.heldState: Candidate selection is distinct from signature verification.

steps.action: Verify the token and profile before adopting claims.
steps.heldState: Verified issuer/key reference accompanies accepted token.

negativeCases: A token-supplied jku/x5u is not followed by this profile.
Unknown or ambiguous kid fails according to the declared profile, never falls back to arbitrary keys/issuers.
acceptance: kid is not a key, globally unique identity or proof of trust.
JWKS response/cache and signature check appear as separate artifacts and local events.

scenarios.title: JWKS rotation and bounded refresh
scenarios.goal: Teach availability and key rotation without inventing an RFC-mandated cache lifetime.
preconditions: Explicit demo policy: cache TTL 300s; one in-flight refresh per issuer; minimum 30s refresh interval; bounded negative cache; 2s fetch timeout; no stale-key acceptance after profile freshness limit. These are demo policies, not universal RFC/Kubernetes defaults.

steps.action: Publish old+new public keys before issuing tokens with new kid.
steps.heldState: Cache initially holds old key; issuer retains both signing generations during selected overlap.

steps.action: Receive new kid; if refresh budget allows, perform one coalesced JWKS refresh.
steps.heldState: Pending tokens stay unaccepted; requests share refresh work.

steps.action: Find new key, verify token and claims, then accept.
steps.heldState: Cache revision and token key generation are explicit.

steps.action: After declared lifetime/overlap, retire old key and expire cache entries.
steps.heldState: Retirement is not instantaneous universal token revocation.

negativeCases: Unknown-kid flood is rate/capacity bounded.
Refresh timeout/missing new kid denies that token; an unrelated valid cached-key token follows its own declared freshness policy.
acceptance: Deterministic clock tests cover overlap, timeout and retry budget.
Kubernetes-specific refresh internals must be checked against pinned implementation before claiming identical timings.

scenarios.title: Issuer, audience, time and claim types
scenarios.goal: Show why a valid signature alone is insufficient.
preconditions: Fixed now; configured skew 30s; required iss/sub/aud/exp; demo additionally requires iat; nbf optional. NumericDate represented in seconds.

steps.action: Finish signature verification before trusting claim values.
steps.heldState: Received/decoded claims retained as untrusted evidence.

steps.action: Match exact issuer and intended audience; accept aud string or array only as allowed by profile.
steps.heldState: Issuer/audience observations identify expected and actual values.

steps.action: Evaluate exp, nbf when present, and separately declared iat/max-age policy.
steps.heldState: Clock/skew inputs shown; iat is not itself an expiration time.

steps.action: Validate required strings/arrays/numbers and subject semantics; then build accepted identity.
steps.heldState: Invalid types cannot coerce into an accepted subject/group.

negativeCases: Wrong issuer/audience, expired/not-yet-valid, missing required claim, milliseconds mistaken for seconds, or string exp rejected.
Duplicate claim names are rejected by this stricter demo parser; do not claim every conforming JWT parser must choose that option.
acceptance: Boundary tests use deterministic timestamps and profile-required vs optional badges.
No rule says all registered JWT claims are universally required.

scenarios.title: ID tokens, access tokens and cross-JWT substitution
scenarios.goal: Teach purpose-specific validation and the Kubernetes ID-token integration as a deliberate profile.
preconditions: OIDC client audience demo-native; ordinary API audience https://api.demo.example; RFC9068 access-token typ at+jwt; separate validators.

steps.action: Issue ID token for client authentication and access token for resource access.
steps.heldState: Different exact artifacts, audiences, lifetimes and intended consumers.

steps.action: Client validates ID token including transaction nonce when used.
steps.heldState: Client login state is distinct from API authorization.

steps.action: Ordinary API applies RFC9068 type, issuer, audience and authorization profile.
steps.heldState: ID-token substitution fails this resource profile.

steps.action: Link to K8S01, whose configured OIDC integration deliberately sends an appropriate ID token as bearer credential.
steps.heldState: No inference that all APIs accept ID tokens, or every access token is a JWT.

negativeCases: Wrong-purpose token with a valid signature rejected using mutually exclusive profile rules.
A typ value alone never proves purpose; compare expected audience/issuer and required claims too.
acceptance: Do not invent mandatory typ=id_token in OIDC Core or K8s.
Do not assert the API server universally distinguishes ID vs access tokens by their origin; show which actual configured check fails.

scenarios.title: Bearer possession, replay and validation lifetime
scenarios.goal: Separate token validity, proof of possession and current server-side status.
preconditions: Bearer profile over TLS; opaque-token comparison uses authenticated RFC7662 introspection; no DPoP/mTLS claim.

steps.action: Send same valid bearer token twice within validity interval.
steps.heldState: Each request obtains received credential; jti alone creates no replay cache.

steps.action: Local validator checks JWT with cached keys and context.
steps.heldState: No automatic revocation call or issuer session check occurs per request.

steps.action: For opaque comparison, API authenticates to introspection and evaluates active plus intended resource/profile.
steps.heldState: Introspection result has explicit cache TTL and evaluation time.

steps.action: Advance clock or change introspection status; show differing rejection points.
steps.heldState: Rejected requests produce no new authorization grant; prior completed actions are not undone.

negativeCases: Do not present signing or JWE encryption as sender binding.
Introspection timeout follows declared fail-closed policy; cached results remain bounded by declared policy.
acceptance: Logout does not imply immediate invalidation of every self-contained JWT.
Link existing sender-constrained flows if available instead of duplicating them; distinguish OAuth bearer errors from K8s Status responses.

scenarios.title: Human OIDC login to kubectl API read
scenarios.goal: Show the complete client login, token authentication and authorized Kubernetes read.
preconditions: Pinned cluster fixture; exec credential API client.authentication.k8s.io/v1; public native OIDC client kubernetes-demo; authorization code + S256 PKCE; Alice sub alice and group readers.

steps.action: kubectl calls exec plugin; plugin opens system browser at issuer and validates returned state; redeems code with verifier; validates ID token/nonce.
steps.heldState: Plugin owns PKCE verifier/state/nonce; issuer credentials stay at issuer; refresh token remains plugin-local.

steps.action: Plugin returns ExecCredential status.token and expirationTimestamp.
steps.heldState: kubectl obtains ID token only; API server never receives refresh token, code or PKCE verifier.

steps.action: kubectl sends Authorization: Bearer ID-token over TLS; API validates configured issuer/key/audience/expiry and maps identity.
steps.heldState: API request userInfo appears only after validation; no browser redirect originates at API server.

steps.action: GET /api/v1/namespaces/demo-dev/pods becomes list/core/pods/demo-dev; reader binding permits Alice.
steps.heldState: Local RBAC decision records matched subject, binding and rule.

steps.action: Read storage through API server and return PodList; mark admission not applicable to reads.
steps.heldState: Result bytes reach kubectl; token validity has not granted blanket access.

negativeCases: Wrong PKCE verifier/state/nonce stops client login.
No matching reader binding yields 403 after successful authentication.
acceptance: A cache-hit second request has no interactive login or per-request issuer introspection.
No API-server password form, automatic browser launch, or implicit Kubernetes User object creation.

scenarios.goal: Keep failed credential validation outside RBAC and admission.
preconditions: OIDC ID-token profile audience kubernetes-demo; RS256 fixtures; unknown-key refresh semantics labeled as implementation-specific; link JWT04-JWT07.

steps.action: Receive a bearer token for a pod request.

steps.action: Evaluate configured issuer discovery, key/signature, audience, expiry and claim/user validation.

steps.action: Use old/new issuer keys to exercise cache hit and unknown-kid refresh.

steps.action: Return Kubernetes 401 Status for an invalid presented bearer credential in this isolated authenticator fixture.

preconditions: demo-dev Role reader: core pods get/list/watch; RoleBinding read-pods subjects Group team:readers; Alice member, Bob not.

steps.action: Accept either user token and show exact userInfo.
steps.heldState: Valid identities persist only for the corresponding request.

steps.action: Validate Bob group membership in both configured groups.

steps.heldState: Display contributing rules; there is no RBAC deny rule overriding another grant.

steps.action: Allow a request when at least one applicable matching rule grants it.
steps.heldState: Store matched-grant explanation, not a guessed generic role label.

steps.action: For secrets get, no rule matches; all demo authorizers have no opinion and overall request is denied.
steps.heldState: Return 403; retain no secret data.

negativeCases: Removing one grant does not remove access still granted by another binding.
A nonmatching restrictive-looking role does not subtract permissions; a JWT group alone grants none.
acceptance: Keep RBAC additive union distinct from sequential multi-authorizer chain semantics in K8S16.
system:authenticated is membership, not automatic admin permission.

steps.action: Authorized kubelet requests token for reader, audience and Pod binding.

steps.action: API issues signed JWT with subject, issuer, audiences, lifetime and binding identifiers.

steps.action: Kubelet writes projection; workload reads token file and calls API over TLS.

scenarios.goal: Compare current bound-object checks with offline cryptographic validation.

steps.action: External service calls TokenReview using its own reviewer credential, with presented token in spec.token and expected audience in spec.audiences.

steps.action: Compare separate validator using trusted cluster discovery/JWKS, signature and issuer/audience/time.

scenarios.title: Remote MCP: discovery to authorized tool result
scenarios.scope: Core MCP 2026-07-28 HTTP authorization teaching profile; authorization itself is optional for MCP deployments. No deprecated session or DCR default.
scenarios.goal: Follow one complete human-delegated request, identifying who issues the token and who finally decides to run the tool.
preconditions: MCP 2026-07-28 over HTTPS Streamable HTTP; canonical resource https://mcp.lab.example/team/mcp.
Public desktop client is already registered at A; redirect is an approved loopback callback, no embedded client secret.
A advertises S256; lab scope files:read is illustrative, not a standardized MCP-wide scope.
steps: C sends a self-contained tools/list POST with correct current-version metadata but no token; R returns 401 with Bearer resource_metadata and files:read guidance.
C obtains and validates resource metadata, selects A, then separately obtains validated A metadata. Label discovery as configuration discovery, not authentication success.
C creates per-attempt state, verifier and S256 challenge; B carries the authorization request with resource and requested scope to A.
A performs its chosen user authentication and consent; depict those as A-owned local/interaction steps, not an MCP password exchange.
B returns a short-lived code. C checks transaction/issuer/redirect binding, then sends grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, code, verifier and resource to the recorded token endpoint.
After A validates the grant, C acquires an access token; C sends it in Authorization on the retried POST.
R separately recovers, validates and authorizes the request; then returns a tool list. A later approved read tool call returns a result only after its own policy decision.
negativeCases: User cancels consent: no token or tool execution.
Missing token on a later POST: challenge again; an earlier successful request grants no connection-wide authority.
No advertised PKCE capability: stop before opening the authorization flow.
acceptance: Show token receipt before R validation and validation before tool execution.
Verifier never appears in browser authorization parameters or at R.
Resource parameter is visible on both authorization and token requests; access token is absent from URLs.
Full and filtered replay converge on the same accepted-result state.

scenarios.title: Discover the correct resource and authorization server
scenarios.scope: Core MCP 2026-07-28 HTTP authorization teaching profile; authorization itself is optional for MCP deployments. No deprecated session or DCR default.
scenarios.goal: Make challenge precedence, path-aware discovery and issuer-isolated credentials observable before any secret is sent.
preconditions: Resource path is /team/mcp; authorization issuer is https://login.lab.example/tenant-a.
Two metadata variants: explicit challenge pointer; no pointer with well-known fallback.
A2 is a separately configured issuer, not an alias of A.
steps: Parse WWW-Authenticate; prefer its resource_metadata URI when present.
Without a pointer, try the path-specific protected-resource well-known URI, then its root fallback; show both exact requests and outcomes.
Validate the recovered resource identifier before using authorization_servers; select one issuer under the profile policy.
For a path-bearing issuer, try OAuth metadata path insertion, OIDC path insertion, then OIDC path appending in the MCP-defined order.
Check metadata issuer equality; bind selected endpoints/capabilities to the same issuer record.

Change resource metadata from A to A2. Keep existing A credentials/tokens isolated; obtain applicable A2 registration rather than forwarding A secrets. CIMD URL portability does not make A tokens portable.
negativeCases: Mismatched resource or issuer: metadata is unusable and no credential request follows.
All permitted discovery endpoints fail: explain the missing document instead of inventing /authorize or /token.
A valid JSON document without required authorization-server information is rejected.
A2 receives neither A refresh token nor A client secret.
acceptance: Inspector distinguishes received JSON, validated metadata and selected issuer.
Record the actual attempted URLs and exact reason for fallback.
Header presence has precedence; tests include multiple challenges and quoted parameter parsing.
Resource canonicalization and issuer exact comparison are separate operations.

scenarios.title: Registration choices: CIMD and existing client registration
scenarios.scope: Core HTTP authorization registration choices: issuer-specific pre-registration or advertised CIMD. RFC7591 DCR is deprecated MCP compatibility only, never the default or a universal requirement.
scenarios.goal: Explain how a client becomes known to an authorization server without suggesting that registration grants resource access.
preconditions: CIMD profile uses an HTTPS client_id with a nonempty path and A advertises client_id_metadata_document_supported.
Sibling profile has a valid pre-registered client ID at the same issuer.
DCR is available only as a visibly labeled compatibility variant, with registration_endpoint explicitly advertised.
steps: Apply the declared choice order: usable existing registration first; otherwise advertised CIMD.
For CIMD, A obtains a synthetic metadata document from the client_id URL, validates required members and exact client_id identity, and checks the requested redirect against that document.
A records the allowed redirect/client authentication method; show that this is registration trust, not proof that a particular user approved access.
Resume MCP01 with the established client ID and a fresh authorization transaction.
Compatibility comparison: when explicitly selected and supported, display RFC7591 request/response, application_type and registration failure handling; never make DCR the default.
If no supported mechanism or configured registration exists, stop with a useful configuration action; do not fabricate credentials.
negativeCases: CIMD client_id differs from its document URL.
Requested redirect absent from metadata, malformed JSON, unavailable document or disallowed trust domain.
Public client incorrectly configured to rely on a packaged secret.
DCR compatibility branch uses incompatible native/web redirect rules or registration fails.
acceptance: CIMD is labeled draft-based and DCR deprecated compatibility for this MCP revision.
A registration object and later consent/grant objects have different exact IDs and authority states.
Client names/logos are untrusted display metadata; approval UI identifies redirect hostname.
Registration choice/retry preserves focus and clearly exposes why setup cannot continue.

scenarios.title: Reject a substituted authorization response
scenarios.scope: Core MCP 2026-07-28 HTTP authorization teaching profile; authorization itself is optional for MCP deployments. No deprecated session or DCR default.
scenarios.goal: Compare code interception, request confusion and issuer mix-up without treating PKCE, state and issuer checks as interchangeable.
preconditions: A completed metadata validation and C retained issuer, verifier, redirect and state in one transaction record.
Primary profile advertises authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported=true.
Use synthetic callbacks; the offline app never opens the supplied redirect.
steps: Run an authorization request with S256, state and exact registered redirect binding.
Deliver a callback to C but retain it as unaccepted input.
Validate state and the response issuer against the recorded transaction; only then permit code redemption at the recorded token endpoint.
A compares the verifier-derived challenge and rejects a substituted verifier or reused code.
Show a separate mismatch branch ending before redemption, and a token-endpoint rejection branch ending after the request but before token issuance.
Exercise the four advertised/present-iss combinations required by the pinned MCP response-validation table.
negativeCases: Wrong state, wrong issuer, missing advertised iss, or unexpected callback redirect.
Present mismatching iss even when support was not advertised: reject.
Both advertisement and iss absent: do not falsely claim MCP requires rejection; retain other transaction checks.
Mismatched issuer in an error response: do not display attacker-controlled error_description/error_uri as trusted AS output.
Wrong verifier, reused code or PKCE downgrade attempt.
acceptance: No code is sent to an endpoint selected from the unvalidated callback.
Exact issuer comparison does not case-fold, remove ports or normalize trailing slashes.
Each failed check names the responsible actor and denied next action.
The PKCE fixture computes the S256 value against an independent known vector.

scenarios.title: A received token is not yet an accepted request
scenarios.scope: Core HTTP resource validation with two declared implementation profiles: RFC9068 JWT or RFC7662 opaque-token introspection. Neither token format is universally required by MCP.
scenarios.goal: Show the resource server validating a token and then authorizing one operation; contrast declared JWT and opaque-token profiles.
preconditions: Two explicit profiles: RFC9068 JWT access token; opaque token with authenticated RFC7662 introspection.
R has an issuer/audience/key or introspection configuration derived from a trusted operator profile.
Link to the dedicated JWT family for full JWS/JWK mechanics; do not require JWT for all MCP deployments.
steps: C sends a token in the request header; show TLS receipt and application recovery as distinct moments.
JWT branch parses claims without trusting them, then validates the selected token profile and intended audience.
Opaque branch sends the token to the configured introspection endpoint using R credentials; receiving a JSON response is distinct from accepting active status and applicable permissions.
Create an R-local validated authorization context only after the profile checks succeed.
Evaluate the required scope and operation-specific resource policy against that context.
Return result or the appropriate invalid-token/permission response, with client knowledge changing only on its receipt.
negativeCases: ID token or token for another API supplied instead of an MCP access token.
Wrong issuer/audience, invalid JWT signature, expired token or opaque active=false.
Introspection unavailable: deny protected work under the declared fail-closed profile; do not invent active status.
Valid token but denied file ACL: token validation remains successful while operation is denied.
acceptance: Decode, verification, scope decision and operation result have distinct state/observations.
JWT token bytes and decoded claims remain related representations; parsing alone creates no verified identity.
401 and 403 are not conflated; introspection credentials never reach C.
Rejected tokens cannot cause a tool side effect or protected result disclosure.

scenarios.title: Insufficient scope and bounded incremental consent
scenarios.scope: Core MCP 2026-07-28 HTTP authorization teaching profile; authorization itself is optional for MCP deployments. No deprecated session or DCR default.
scenarios.goal: Explain why a valid read token cannot authorize a write, and how the client can request a deliberate upgrade.
preconditions: C previously requested and received files:read; new tool operation requires files:write.
The profile implements the current MCP scope-challenge behavior; scope names remain application-defined.
Authorization may be declined; no silent approval is modeled.
steps: R validates the read token, then rejects the write with 403 and Bearer insufficient_scope plus operation-required scopes.
C parses the challenge and shows the extra requested permission before launching a new authorization attempt.
Build the reauthorization scope set from the previously requested set and current challenge; retain exact requested versus granted sets.
A asks for appropriate consent and may return a smaller grant or a denial.
C retries with the new token only after successful grant processing; R reevaluates the write policy.
Bound retries and end with a useful permanent-error explanation when permissions still do not satisfy the operation.
negativeCases: Challenge scopes are not necessarily a subset of PRM scopes_supported.
Missing challenge scope uses the selected MCP initial-scope fallback only where applicable; do not infer unlimited access.
User declines, AS grants less, repeated challenge, or a broader scope hierarchy does not satisfy the local policy.
A scope upgrade does not override a separate per-object ACL denial.
acceptance: Old token remains a historical/read-authorized object; it is not rewritten into a write token.
Consent denial prevents write execution without erasing unrelated accepted read state.
Test union calculation and retry limit independently of runtime-generated expectations.
Copy clearly separates 401 sign-in need from 403 additional permission.

scenarios.title: Expiry, refresh rotation and reauthorization
scenarios.scope: Core HTTP token-lifetime lesson; refresh issuance is discretionary. Public-client rotation is selected for this MCP baseline. RFC7009 revocation is a separately advertised optional profile.
scenarios.goal: Follow credential lifetime through renewal failure as well as success, with endpoint-specific knowledge.
actors: User/browser B when reauthorization is needed
preconditions: Public-client profile with short-lived access token and AS-issued rotating refresh token.
Sibling input issues no refresh token; issuance is not guaranteed.
Clock, rotation and optional revocation propagation are fixed synthetic fixtures.
steps: Advance time until the access token expires; local expiry prediction or an R 401 starts renewal without accepting the expired token.
C sends refresh token only to A, bound to its client/resource grant; A checks validity and grant constraints.
On success, A issues a new access/refresh generation and invalidates the prior refresh generation under the selected rotation policy.
C acquires the replacement before updating its current credential store; replay exposes old/new exact IDs and retention separately.
On invalid_grant, missing refresh token or revocation, discard unusable current credentials and offer a new authorization-code flow.
Optional advertised RFC7009 branch separates C revocation request, A invalidation and R knowledge/propagation; disconnect alone does not imply token revocation.
negativeCases: Reuse of a rotated refresh token; attempted scope/resource escalation through refresh.
Refresh rejection or transient network failure must not cause unbounded loops.
offline_access is not an MCP resource permission and cannot be assumed supported or sufficient to obtain refresh.
A revoked self-contained token may not be known immediately to an offline validator; expose the declared enforcement policy.
acceptance: Refresh token never appears at R, in a URL, or in exported diagnostic text.
Old token possession, AS invalidation and R rejection are distinct facts.
Public-client rotation is shown for this MCP profile; generic OAuth alternatives are not silently substituted.
Expiry and renewal are repeatable under a deterministic clock.

scenarios.title: OAuth permission, tool approval and resource policy
scenarios.scope: Core per-request HTTP authorization plus separately declared host approval and resource ACL policies; the host UI is not a protocol grant.
scenarios.goal: Distinguish identity evidence, a transport access grant, a host decision to invoke a tool, and the server decision for the target object.
preconditions: C already holds a valid scoped token; no new login is needed.
The lab host requires explicit approval for its synthetic destructive tool.
The server has a separate per-object policy; this approval UI is a declared host policy, not a new OAuth grant.
steps: List tools under the authorization supplied on that request; show that a listed capability is not a promised successful mutation.
The model proposes a tool call; C displays concrete tool/target/arguments for the host approval decision.
If U declines, C sends no tools/call and retains the OAuth token unchanged.
If U approves, C sends a fresh authenticated POST; R validates its authorization and P checks the chosen target.
Return either a policy denial with no side effect or a completed operation result.
Contrast AS sign-in/consent with this host approval and server authorization on separate cards.
negativeCases: Valid grant plus user denial; user approval plus ACL denial; untrusted tool annotations pretending an operation is harmless.
Changed arguments after approval invalidate the declared host approval record.
Self-asserted MCP clientInfo/capabilities cannot substitute for authentication.
Cached tool list from another authorization context must not bypass the current request decision.
acceptance: Expose independent booleans for tokenAccepted, hostInvocationApproved, resourceAuthorized and operationExecuted.
Denied invocation creates no fictitious network exchange.
No OIDC ID token or universal subject claim is invented merely because OAuth is used.
Keyboard users can inspect the concrete operation and decline without losing journey focus.

scenarios.title: MCP proxy: a separate OAuth grant for the upstream API
scenarios.scope: Optional deployment topology using core HTTP authorization on the MCP boundary and an independent upstream OAuth grant; not mandatory for every server.
scenarios.goal: Show both trust boundaries and the two different access tokens when an MCP server calls another protected service.
preconditions: C-to-P authorization already uses a token with P as resource.
P is separately registered as an OAuth client at UAS; no upstream token is initially available.
Use two collapsed chapters so only one authorization boundary is expanded at a time.
